(1) the optimum Se implantation conditions for the fabrication of GaAs FET’s are 150 keV Se+ implantation and 850 degrees C annealing, (2) the optimum encapsulating layer for the annealing of the Se implantation is Ga2O3 + Al, (3) the optimum annealing temperature for the Se implantation in semi-insulating LEC GaAs is 850 degrees C.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a process for the fabrication of high quality GaAs FET devices using ion implantation.
the development of GaAs FET technology using ion implantation for device fabrication.
the characterisation and optimisation of the implantation parameters and encapsulation layers for Se implanted GaAs substrates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best implantation parameters for Se are 100 keV, 5 x 1014 ions/cm2 and annealing at 900 degrees C for 10 min.
the best results in terms of mobility are obtained by using SiO2 encapsulating layers, and that the best results for uniformity are obtained by using Ga2O3 + Al as encapsulating layer.
Se implantation is not a suitable technique for producing semi-insulating layers in GaAs for device fabrication.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Se implanted layers are characterised by a high doping efficiency, a high uniformity of doping, and a high mobility.
for a given Se dose, the doping profile of implanted Se is not affected by the encapsulating layer, but for a given ion energy the doping efficiency is affected.
the best results for Se ion implantation are obtained with 150 keV Se ions, 900 °C annealing, 30 s RTA and SiO2 encapsulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Se implantation process is a very promising alternative for obtaining semi-insulating substrates with a high resistivity.
the use of Ga2O3 + Al as encapsulating layer is the best choice in terms of doping profile, uniformities and mobility.
the use of Ga2O3 + Al encapsulation is the most promising for the fabrication of GaAs MESFETs.
